title: Aszú and puttonyos
subtitle: The great sweet wine
objectives: Explain how Tokaji Aszú is made

steps.title: Aszú berries
steps.body: Aszú berries are grapes shrivelled by noble rot, picked one by one, often in several passes. They're collected and kept as a paste or whole. Then they're soaked in fermenting must or a base wine for 12 to 60 hours, extracting sugar and flavour. The mixture is pressed and fermented slowly, sometimes for months.
steps.highlight: Botrytised berries soaked in base wine

steps.title: Puttonyos
steps.body: Traditionally, sweetness was measured in puttonyos: the number of puttony, 25 kg hods of aszú berries, added to a 136-litre Gönci barrel of base wine, from 3 to 6. Since 2013, Tokaji Aszú must have at least 120 g/l of sugar, equal to the old 5 puttonyos; puttonyos labels of 5 and 6 are optional. Aszú ages at least 18 months in oak.

steps.prompt: Put the making of Tokaji Aszú in order.
items: Pick botrytised berries one by one
Soak in base wine or must
steps.explanation: Selection, soaking and slow fermentation give Aszú.

steps.title: Taste
steps.body: Tokaji Aszú is golden to amber, with apricot, orange marmalade, honey, saffron, ginger and tea. Sugar is balanced by Furmint's searing acidity, so it never feels cloying. It ages for decades, even a century or more.

steps.prompt: What is the minimum sugar for Tokaji Aszú since 2013?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Aszú berries are soaked in base wine, then fermented slowly
Since 2013, Aszú needs at least 120 g/l of sugar
